subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix prioritize a pi-tui renderer/dependency change, OpenClaw-owned viewport/follow anchoring, or an explicit TUI auto-scroll preference?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the durable fix affects terminal UX policy and third-party renderer ownership rather than being a narrow code-only repair.

options.title: Fix renderer and anchoring
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven full redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add a TUI auto-scroll setting
options.body: Expose explicit user control for terminal follow behavior, accepting a new settings surface plus fresh-install and upgrade proof burden.

options.title: Hold for live repro first
options.body: Keep implementation paused until a current-main PTY capture demonstrates the exact jump and renderer reason.

recommendation.title: Fix renderer and anchoring
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven full redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.
